what: Design item, not for now unless you take it: macOS patch code with no trap per patch. Today each patch's code is a page swap on macOS (`blaze-live` `slots/macos.rs` `swap`: `mach_vm_allocate`, `mach_vm_protect`, `mach_vm_remap`, `mach_vm_deallocate`, a copy of whole 16 KiB pages, a shootdown, `sys_icache_invalidate`): about 8 to 10 us against Linux's 0 system calls. The Linux way (a second, writable mapping of the region) is not open on Apple Silicon: the kernel keeps executable pages outside `MAP_JIT` from being writable through another mapping (.NET 7's W^X found double mapping unusable there and uses `MAP_JIT` with `pthread_jit_write_protect_np`), and `MAP_JIT` can't be mapped at the image's fixed region (`MAP_JIT | MAP_FIXED` is refused). The way to the bound: the runtime maps a `MAP_JIT` region where the kernel puts it (within +-4 GiB of the image, as adrp reaches; checked, else `Live::start` says so), names it to the linker (a new `Answer` kind in `blaze-live` `patch.rs`, which this lane writes once the linker side is agreed), and the linker lays patch code out there instead of in `__blaze_patch`. A write is then `pthread_jit_write_protect_np(0)`, the copy, `(1)` and `sys_icache_invalidate`: no trap. Needs hardware to check before it is built; blaze-live's side is small once the linker places code at a runtime-named region.
why: Needs Apple Silicon hardware to check MAP_JIT placement within adrp reach before it is built; no hardware in this lane. Recorded as a design item in speed-of-light.md (speed-sol2-link).
